Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is highly plausible given the setting (possible recent antipsychotic exposure), rigidity may be masked by somnolence, but autonomic instability and altered consciousness align; it often presents with hyperthermia and fluctuating consciousness. Serotonin syndrome overlaps significantly but typically includes more prominent neuromuscular signs (clonus, hyperreflexia, tremor)—less emphasized here, though still likely if recent SSRI/SNRI or MAOI exposure. Heat stroke is compelling given environmental context (undressing in extreme heat), altered mental status, and autonomic dysregulation—but requires ruling out primary CNS drivers, as isolated heat stroke rarely causes profound paranoia or persistent unresponsiveness without severe core hyperthermia (>40°C) and multiorgan involvement. Acute schizophrenia exacerbation with catatonia is included because of paranoia and refusal to engage, but the somnolence, autonomic dysregulation, and lack of typical agitation make primary psychiatric etiology less likely without concurrent medical illness; thus ranked lowest among top five. All differentials require urgent labs (CBC, CMP, CK, ABG, tox screen, lactate, blood cultures), core temperature, ECG, and neuroimaging if focal signs emerge."}
